correctness.rationale: For finite beta the aligned- and opposed-neighbor rates are positive. The even part has detailed balance against the periodic Gibbs law; the odd part contributes a telescoping difference of adjacent bond variables to total inflow minus outflow. Irreducibility yields the unique Gibbs stationary distribution. Aligned neighbors give zero log stationary flux ratio, and opposed neighbors give −4 beta K times the left bond. The latter bond is fair conditional on the opposed neighbors; the conditional weighted log is 2 beta K gamma_o, so the rate per spin is beta K gamma_o(1−C2). Under Gibbs the bond variables are tilted independent signs of mean z conditioned on product +1, giving C2=(z²+z^(N−2))/(1+z^N). In the lag difference the even terms cancel and the odd term is +gamma_o(1−C2) with the specified right-minus-left sign. Twelve fresh finite-ring bond-support checks confirm all three identities. In the infinite-chain objective x*tanh(p x)*sech²x the log derivative is strictly decreasing in x from +infinity to −2 and decreases strictly in p at every positive x. Its unique zero is the global maximum, decreasing in p for x*=beta*J. Its limit at infinity solves 2x tanh x=1 by uniform decay of the additional log-derivative term on x at or above that positive bound. Continuity in p gives the endpoint at p=2; independent high-precision roots match both constants.
residual_risks: The optimum and its bounds are for thermodynamic-limit entropy and dimensionless x, not a universal finite-ring optimizer or an ordering in unscaled beta when J varies. The entropy is a path rate, not the derivative of stationary Shannon entropy.

originality.rationale: The generator, Gibbs-invariance mechanism and lag slope as a correlation observable are established or directly implicit in prior directed-Glauber work; in particular the large-bias rate already occurs in Godrèche–Luck (2015), not just in the cited 2024 papers. The distinct claim is the explicit stationary path-entropy evaluation at every stated ring size, its identification with the lag slope, and the sharp thermodynamic temperature optimum along this fixed-coupling path. Same-date entropy records cover a three-spin case and a zero-reciprocity boundary, not this combined theorem. This is not a priority claim for the model or strong regime.
residual_risks: The finite entropy evaluation is short once the older generator and Gibbs law are known; another treatment could encode it in a domain-wall current or an entropy-flux calculation. The keyword misses and bounded web lookup are not proof of absence.
The frozen comparison should not be read as claiming exclusion of K>J from Godrèche–Luck (2015), or a new lag propagator.

value.rationale: The Gibbs law is insensitive to the odd rate, so a stationary observable cannot diagnose this particular arrow of time through configuration weights alone. A closed finite-ring dissipation density and its quantitative calibration by initial left/right lag distinguish dynamics on that common law. The unique sharp dimensionless temperature window and limiting endpoints tell when dissipation is largest along a fixed coupling ratio; those do not follow as a physical interpretation from stationarity alone. The combination is worthwhile without claiming a new Ising dynamics or a general thermodynamic bound.
residual_risks: No claim about maximum dissipation at finite N, at fixed arbitrary V, in a different update process, or in a different model.
